subject: general
question: Which of the following statements best explains kinetic energy?

options.text: It is the energy an object has because of its motion, and it increases as the object's speed increases.
It is the energy stored in an object due to its shape.
It is the energy an object has because it is at rest.
It is the energy that decreases as the object's speed increases.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is the energy an object has because of its motion, and it increases as the object's speed increases.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Kinetic Energy** is a type of energy that an object possesses due to its motion. It is defined as **the work needed to accelerate an object from rest to its current velocity**.
 
• The formula for kinetic energy is **KE = 1/2 mv²**, where **m** is the mass of the object and **v** is its velocity.
 
• The energy increases with the square of the speed. For example, if the speed of an object doubles, its kinetic energy increases by four times.
 
• Kinetic energy is **directly proportional to the mass** of the moving object. Larger masses result in higher kinetic energy at the same velocity.
 
• This energy type is critical in various applications like **transportation, machinery, and sports**, where motion is a key factor.
 
• Statement "**It is the energy an object has because of its motion, and it increases as the object's speed increases**" is correct because it aligns with the definition and principles of kinetic energy.
